modelingNotes: OSM (way 20326709, bundled): footprint outline (about 12 x 12 m with the buttress bulges on the west/east faces), height 52 m, building:levels 13, heritage stone. The base storey is extruded from that exact polygon; every upper storey steps back inside it (registration and total height 52 m kept).

Published facts (Wikipedia/Structurae, reviewed Commons photos 00-05): flamboyant Gothic tower built 1509-1523, about 52 m without the statue, four storeys above the ground arches; open pointed arches at ground level on all four faces; corner buttress piers with niches that step back with weathered caps; two rows of paired lancets (a short row and a tall belfry row) separated by a tracery band; central buttress on each face; blind-tracery crown under a cornice and balustrade; corner pedestals with the beasts of the evangelists; St James statue on the north-west corner pinnacle.

Inferred from photo proportions scaled to 52 m: stage breaks at 10.4, 24.1, 31.5-33, 36.6 and 48.3 m, arch size 3.6 x 8 m, bay and lancet widths. Statuary, crockets and tracery cusps are abstract masses; gargoyles are simple spouts. The Pascal statue inside the base is not modelled.
